name: Cement, blocks, pavers and precast
shape_facts: Block/paver plant, precast yard, readymix batching plant, or cement dealer/distributor.
Manual/semi-automatic machines vs fully automatic plant; number of machines and moulds.
Daily output (blocks, square feet of pavers, cubic metres of concrete).
Sells to contractors, individual home builders, developers, or government projects.
Own trucks/transit mixers and drivers vs hired.
Yard space for curing and finished stock.
Cement, aggregate and sand bought on credit or cash.
scope_rule: pi notes business problems: material stock, mix consumption, breakage, curing space, orders and deliveries, contractor credit, drivers, machines and reporting. It gives no mix-design, strength, structural, curing-science or site-safety advice, and no opinion on whether products meet a standard or a test result. It records roles (contractor, driver, site engineer), not people’s names or numbers. Accidents with machines, trucks or collapses mean pi stops and points to emergency services.

vocabulary.ret / sand: sand, often by truckload or cubic feet
vocabulary.taraai / curing: keeping blocks/concrete wet as they harden

problems.phrase: Cement goes out of the store faster than blocks come out — something’s off
Breakage during loading and transport, contractor refuses broken pieces
Customer says blocks are weak and cracked, wants money back
Curing yard is full so we have to stop production
Cement rate went up but I already gave contractor the old rate
Contractors take material on credit and disappear after the project
I don’t know actual cement used per 100 blocks
Sand and bajri trucks deliver short but we pay full
Readymix truck reached late, concrete set, customer angry
Drivers do side trips and diesel usage doesn’t add up
Diesel cost per delivery keeps climbing
Orders come on calls, nobody writes the site address properly, wrong delivery
Machine moulds wear out and nobody planned replacement
Daily output count from the supervisor is just a number on WhatsApp
Labour works on daily wage, attendance is a mess
Rain or heat ruins a day’s batch
Old design pavers lying in the yard for a year
Government project payments come months late
Tendering paperwork takes days every time
Few new leads — builders only come through old contacts
No photos of our paver designs online, customers can’t see options
Cash from walk-in buyers handled by the munshi, never matches
Block machine operator left and output dropped
I don’t know which sites have pending deliveries today

material use: How many bags of cement do you use in a day?
How do you check that against blocks produced?
breakage and quality: Where does most breakage happen — loading, transport or at site?
How are complaints about strength handled?
capacity: What limits output most — machines, labour or curing space?
How many days does stock sit before dispatch?
orders and delivery: How are deliveries scheduled each day?
How often does a truck go to the wrong place?
credit: How many contractors buy on credit?
trucks and diesel: How many trucks or transit mixers do you run?
How is diesel issued and checked?
suppliers: Do sand and bajri loads get checked on arrival?
reporting: How do you get the day’s production and sales numbers?

seasons: PK building season after monsoon through spring; monsoon (July–September) stops sites and floods yards; extreme heat (May–June) affects curing; Ramadan and Eid slowdowns; fiscal-year-end (June) government spending rush. UAE: cooler months (October–April) peak; summer midday ban slows sites; Ramadan shorter working hours. Canada: April–November construction season; winter cold-weather concreting limits and heated enclosures; spring road-restriction periods limit heavy truck loads.
care: No mix design, strength, curing method or structural advice; note “complaints of weak blocks” only as a business problem.
Accidents (crush injuries, truck accidents, wall collapse) — stop and point to emergency services.
No opinions on test reports or standards compliance; do not help alter cube-test results or certificates — decline.
Sand/aggregate from unauthorised mining: pi does not help source or hide it.
Drivers and labour: roles and counts only, no names, licences or IDs.
Government tender bribery or “settings” requests: decline plainly.
build_ideas: Daily production log by product type, entered from the yard on phone, with cement bags issued alongside.
Material consumption ratio report: cement, sand and aggregate used per unit produced, with exceptions flagged.
Yard stock board by product, design, colour and age, including curing status.
Order book with site location pin, quantity, delivery date and contact role.
Delivery scheduler for trucks/transit mixers with trip status from drivers.
Diesel issue and trip log per vehicle with distance, compared against expected usage.
Breakage and return register by stage (loading, transport, site).
Contractor credit ledger with limits, ageing and project-linked balances.
Incoming material check: truck photo, volume estimate and weighbridge slip logged on arrival.
Machine and mould maintenance calendar with usage counts.
Daily-wage attendance and output register for labour.
Paver design catalogue page and WhatsApp catalogue for customers to choose from.

exchange.text: Mera masla yeh hai ke cement ki boriyan khatam ho jati hain lekin blocks utne nahi bante.
